text:
meera: Heads-up — CloudLedger (dedicated) is seeing tail latency regressions after enabling continuous batching. P95 looks fine but p99 spikes on longer sequences. I profiled a few requests and it looks like kernel selection is falling back to a slower path and KV cache churn increases when queue length grows. Can we propose a tenant-specific batching guard (queue cap + token window) for Dedicated? cc @alex @jon :eyes:

alex: Can you paste the profiling snippet? curious about sequence lengths and kernel fingerprints.

meera: Sure, quick extract from the perf run (trimmed):
```
request_id: cl-2026-08-12-01
seq_len: 1536
kernel: fallback_attention_v2
KB_hits_before: 120
KB_evictions_during: 43
latency_ms: 1187 (p99)
baseline_kernel: fast_attention_v1 (when seq_len <= 1024)
```
KV cache eviction spikes line up with bursts of large seq_len requests — we end up flushing shared cache and next requests pay heavy reload cost.

jon: Ok. Two immediate levers: a) enforce a per-tenant in-queue cap to keep effective batch sizes predictable, and b) introduce a token_budget window (sliding) that deprioritizes requests likely to trigger fallback kernels. For Dedicated we can supply a small config patch for CloudLedger: max_queue_items=40, max_batch_token_budget=80000, seq_len_threshold_override=1400 (to force pin to fast kernel if their workloads are mostly <=1400).

samir: Interesting. Forcing kernel pin could reduce correctness if model expects different kernels? Any safety checks?

meera: Good point. This is only for the inference path (no model weight change). It's a runtime kernel selection hint — we'll add an opt-in canary flag so we can revert if we see score drift. Also add a quality gating eval on a small prompt set.

alex: Can you show the config snippet you'd like us to apply to the Dedicated tenant pool? I want to review default QoS interactions.

meera: Draft config below (will wrap in ServiceConfig for Dedicated pool):
```json
{
  "tenant": "cloudledger",
  "queue_cap": 40,
  "token_budget_window": 80000,
  "priority_shedding": {
    "policy": "age_then_tokens",
    "soft_limit_ms": 120,
    "hard_limit_ms": 500
  },
  "kernel_hint": {
    "seq_len_override": 1400,
    "allow_force_pin": true
  },
  "canary": {
    "enabled": true,
    "percent": 10,
    "rollback_on": ["p99_latency_increase", "quality_regression"]
  }
}
```

jon: That looks reasonable. Couple notes: the token_budget is global-per-queue, so 80k should reduce the formation of giant batches but still allow medium bursts. Soft limit_ms helps avoid starving short requests.

samir: Also add a note to kernel selection logic: when kernel_hint.allow_force_pin==true, runtime should still evaluate runtime_memory_pressure and not pin if it would OOM on that instance.

meera: Agreed — will add safety guard + metric emission: kernel_pin_applied and kernel_pin_skipped(reason).

infra-bot: Created ticket RW-44321: "CloudLedger Dedicated — queue & token-budget guard + kernel hint canary" https://redwood-internal/issue/RW-44321

alex: One more ask — can we enable a quick perf trace sampler for the canary group (1 in 20 requests) so we capture kernel fingerprints and KV cache ops? add to the ticket.

meera: Will do. I'll also run a 24h canary and post p50/p95/p99 and KB hit/eviction metrics. If all good, roll to 100% and then we can consider applying similar conservative defaults to other mid-sized Dedicated tenants.

jon: Sounds good. Thanks — I'll queue a review for the config change and add tests for queue policy interactions.

meera: Thanks all. If anyone sees weird regressions ping me directly. :thumbsup:
